examiner_actions: assign documents to a role, with a focus
search the case file for an open question

roles.title: Parties reviewer
roles.mirrors: defense counsel mapping parties and contractor tiers from the records
roles.brief: You are the parties reviewer on a construction claim. You work out, from the records only, who the parties are, what role each had on the project, and how they are related: who contracted with whom, who represented whom, who reviewed whose submittals, who supplied what, who inspected.
roles.default_focus: every organisation and person named, their roles, the relationships between them, and names written differently for the same party
roles.sees: the documents it is assigned, in full

roles.title: Technical reviewer
roles.brief: You are the technical reviewer on a construction claim. You record, from the records only, the design requirements, submittals and how they were dispositioned, tests and their results, deviations from requirements, and when each happened. You state facts, never causes.
roles.default_focus: dated events: design requirements and values, submittals and approvals, tests and results, problems reported, repairs, and what the documents do not contain
roles.sees: the documents it is assigned, in full

verifier_rules: Every quote must be found on the page it cites, after collapsing whitespace and folding curly quotes and dashes. Case, spelling and word order must match.
A quote on a production label (a cover sheet or divider added when the claim file was assembled) is refused.
A quote on a page outside the readable claim file is refused.
An event dated as the document's own date must match the date read from the document, with its source span.
An event dated from the text must have a quote that shows that date.
A party's name must appear in its quotes; a relationship's two parties must both appear in its quotes.
An alias is accepted only when one quote shows both names.
A claim with no citation is shown as interpretation, never as fact.
One failed citation refuses the whole claim. Refused claims are kept with their reasons, not softened.
harness.negative_rule: Each role proposes what the claim file does not contain at the end of the run, with search terms that would find a counter-example. A negative is accepted only if every in-scope page was read in the run and a phrase search for each term finds nothing in scope.

memory_collections.pages / documents / metadata: the ingested claim file, written only by ingestion
memory_collections.coverage: every read and search, with the pages it covered
memory_collections.refusals: refused claims with the verifier's reasons
memory_collections.workers: every reader started: role, documents, focus, tokens
memory_collections.trace: one event per step of the run
memory_collections.checkpoints: LangGraph run state, so a run can stop and resume
memory_collections.outputs: chronology, party map, exhibits and coverage report
memory_collections.cache: Reducto and Gemini responses, so nothing is paid for twice

answer_key.summary: About 11 p.m., the M1 row of anchors in eastbound ceiling module EB081 pulls out. The suspended concrete ceiling swings down onto a passing car, and the passenger is killed.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: As the car approached the end of the I-90 connector tunnel, a section of the tunnel’s suspended concrete ceiling detached from the tunnel roof and fell onto the vehicle.

answer_key.summary: During on-scene work, investigators measure every anchor left in the portal roof. Many have displaced downward, and the displaced share is greatest in the most heavily loaded rows.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: After the accident, 161 of the 634 remaining adhesive anchors supporting the D Street portal ceiling were found to have measurable displacement,

answer_key.summary: The NTSB Materials Laboratory examines the 20 failed M1-row anchors and others from the tunnel. Yellowed epoxy appears only on anchors that had displaced (0.5 inch or more), and on one failed anchor it reaches about 4 inches up the embedment.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: 13 of the 20 anchors in that row showed a yellow discoloration found only on displaced anchors.

answer_key.summary: MIT's FTIR analysis for the NTSB matches all epoxy samples from the tunnel to Powers Fast Set, not Standard Set. An FHWA report states that construction invoices also show a fast-set formula was used.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy at MIT showed that all of the samples from the tunnels, including the samples from the accident site, matched to the Fast Set reference samples.

answer_key.summary: The FHWA runs sustained-load (creep) tests on anchors still installed in the westbound portal roof. In 3 of the 9 rigorous tests the displacement never stabilizes; two anchors pull out completely.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: During the sustained load tests, two anchors pulled completely free of the tunnel roof.

answer_key.summary: In 82-day FHWA laboratory creep tests, anchors set with Power-Fast Fast Set creep at every load, and those loaded to 4,000 lb fail. Standard Set anchors barely move under the same conditions.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The testing showed that anchors installed with the Powers Fast Set epoxy, using best practices, exhibited significant and continued displacement (creep) when subjected to loads as low as 1,000 pounds.

Evaluation reports ER-4514 and ESR-1531 governed the Power-Fast epoxy adhesive anchor systems under ICBO/ICC-ES acceptance criteria AC58. Following the July 10, 2006 ceiling panel collapse in the I-90 connector tunnel, FHWA and NTSB conducted field tension testing, displacement monitoring, and laboratory investigations. Subsequent testing by FHWA, Standard Testing and Engineering Company, Bodycote Polymer, and MIT examined void formation, installation variables, and comparative performance of Fast Set and Standard Set epoxy formulations, documenting rapid creep failure of Fast Set installations during sustained tension tests at elevated temperatures.

decision.summary: Evaluation reports ER-4514 and ESR-1531 governed the Power-Fast epoxy adhesive anchor systems under ICBO/ICC-ES acceptance criteria AC58. Following the July 10, 2006 ceiling panel collapse in the I-90 connector tunnel, FHWA and NTSB conducted field tension testing, displacement monitoring, and laboratory investigations. You state documented facts, never fault or liability.

members.title: Forensic engineer
members.mirrors: the forensic expert retained with the carrier's approval
members.job: You are the forensic engineer retained by defense counsel, with the claim professional's approval. From the records only, you set out the technical record: design requirements and values, submittals and how they were dispositioned, tests with their methods and results, deviations from requirements, repairs, and when each happened. You state documented facts, never an opinion on cause.
members.sees: as counsel, for its own documents and claims
can: as counsel, except asking for an expert
members.waits_for: expert.approved: it cannot start before the lead approves it

members.title: Readers
members.job: Read whole documents (long ones in page windows) for one role and focus; return dated events, parties, relationships, aliases and open questions, each with an exact quote.
members.sees: only their batch (about 40k characters), plus up to 2 short documents it cites by reference number
can: one automatic repair of refused claims

members.title: Dispatcher, verifier, assembly
members.mirrors: the claims system and file rules
members.job: Turns events into tasks and runs them in parallel; checks every claim against the page; tests absences; decides whether the file may close; assembles the chronology, party map and exhibits.
can: hold a task until what it waits for exists
expire stuck tasks and tell the lead
stop the run on a guard

verifier_rules: Every quote must be found on the page it cites. Whitespace, curly quotes and dashes are folded, and a word may be joined across a hyphen at a line break; case, spelling and word order must match.
A quote on a production label (a cover sheet or divider added when the claim file was assembled), or on a page outside the readable claim file, is refused.
An event dated as the document's own date must match the date read from the document; an event dated from the text must have a quote that shows that date.

A party's name must appear in its quotes, ignoring case, punctuation and corporate suffixes; a relationship's two parties must both appear. At assembly, a name also appears through a verified alias quoted in the claim.
An alias is accepted only when one quote shows both names.
A refused claim is sent back to its reader once with the page and the reason; if it still fails it is kept with its reasons, never softened.
team_spec.negative_rule: At the end, each role proposes what the claim file does not contain, with search terms that would find a counter-example. An absence is accepted only if every in-scope page was read in the run and a phrase search for each term finds nothing in scope.

memory.events: the append-only event log: every message between roles, with its cause; change streams wake consumers
memory.tasks: one task per event a role must handle: waits-for, deadline, state, outcome
memory.reservations: which task holds which document, per role (unique index), so no document is read twice by a role
memory.coverage: every page handed to a reader, with the role and focus, logged before the model runs
memory.findings / refusals: verified claims, and refused ones with the verifier's reasons
memory.exclusions: documents the lead ruled out of scope, with its reason
memory.disputes: conflicting claims on the same page and the lead's ruling
memory.model_calls: every model call: who, for which task, tokens, cost, the decision and its reasoning summary
memory.workers: every reader: documents, pages, focus, claims kept and refused
memory.checkpoints: LangGraph state of each role's task (plan, read, review, close), so a task can resume
memory.pages / documents / metadata / sources: the ingested claim file (GridFS for the PDFs, Atlas Search on page text)
memory.cache: model and parser answers, so a finished run replays for free
